### PE_T5_01 (MCQ): In Practice Exam (Topic 5), the metabolic cell body of a neurone containing the nucleus is the:

- A) Axon
- B) Cyton / Soma
- C) Dendrite
- D) Synaptic knob

> **✅ Answer:** B) Cyton / Soma
> **Explanation:** Cyton (Soma) is the main cell body of a neurone.

### PE_T5_02 (MCQ): In Practice Exam (Topic 5), Nissl's granules in cyton and dendrites consist of clumps of:

- A) Smooth ER and lipids
- B) Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum and free Ribosomes
- C) Lysosomes and Golgi bodies
- D) Microtubules and centrioles

> **✅ Answer:** B) Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum and free Ribosomes
> **Explanation:** Nissl's granules are RER and free ribosomes synthesizing protein.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="In Practice Exam (Topic 5), Nissl's gran" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### PE_T5_03 (MCQ): In Practice Exam (Topic 5), Nissl's granules are strictly ABSENT in:

- A) Cyton
- B) Axon and Axon Hillock
- C) Main dendrites
- D) Soma cytoplasm

> **✅ Answer:** B) Axon and Axon Hillock
> **Explanation:** Nissl's granules are absent in axon hillock and axon.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="In Practice Exam (Topic 5), Nissl's gran" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>

### PE_T5_04 (MCQ): In Practice Exam (Topic 5), saltatory nerve impulse propagation leaps along myelinated axons at:

- A) Synaptic knobs
- B) Uninsulated Nodes of Ranvier
- C) Schwann cell nuclei
- D) Axon hillock

> **✅ Answer:** B) Uninsulated Nodes of Ranvier
> **Explanation:** Action potentials jump from Node of Ranvier to Node of Ranvier.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="In Practice Exam (Topic 5), saltatory ne" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>

### PE_T5_05 (MCQ): In Practice Exam (Topic 5), which CNS neuroglia construct the Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB)?

- A) Astrocytes
- B) Oligodendrocytes
- C) Microglia
- D) Ependymal cells

> **✅ Answer:** A) Astrocytes
> **Explanation:** Astrocytes form perivascular end-feet creating the Blood-Brain Barrier.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="In Practice Exam (Topic 5), which CNS ne" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>

### PE_T5_06 (MCQ): In Practice Exam (Topic 5), myelin sheath in the Central Nervous System (CNS) is synthesized by:

- A) Schwann cells
- B) Oligodendrocytes
- C) Astrocytes
- D) Microglia

> **✅ Answer:** B) Oligodendrocytes
> **Explanation:** Oligodendrocytes form CNS myelin; Schwann cells form PNS myelin.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="In Practice Exam (Topic 5), myelin sheat" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>

### PE_T5_07 (MCQ): In Practice Exam (Topic 5), phagocytic macrophage defense neuroglia in the CNS are:

- A) Astrocytes
- B) Microglia
- C) Ependymal cells
- D) Satellite cells

> **✅ Answer:** B) Microglia
> **Explanation:** Microglia act as tissue macrophages defending the CNS.

### PE_T5_08 (MSQ): In Practice Exam (Topic 5 - MSQ), select all neuroglial cells residing in the Central Nervous System (CNS): (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Astrocytes
- [ ] B) Oligodendrocytes
- [ ] C) Microglia
- [ ] D) Ependymal cells
- [ ] E) Schwann cells

> **✅ Answers (Multiple Select):** A) Astrocytes, B) Oligodendrocytes, C) Microglia, D) Ependymal cells
> **Explanation:** CNS neuroglia: Astrocytes, Oligodendrocytes, Microglia, Ependymal. Schwann = PNS.

### PE_T5_09 (MSQ): In Practice Exam (Topic 5 - MSQ), select all neuroglial cells residing in the Peripheral Nervous System (PNS): (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Myelinating Schwann cells
- [ ] B) Ganglionic Satellite cells
- [ ] C) CNS Astrocytes
- [ ] D) CNS Microglia
- [ ] E) CNS Oligodendrocytes

> **✅ Answers (Multiple Select):** A) Myelinating Schwann cells, B) Ganglionic Satellite cells
> **Explanation:** PNS neuroglia include Schwann cells and Satellite cells.

### PE_T5_10 (MSQ): In Practice Exam (Topic 5 - MSQ), select all anatomical locations containing Bipolar Neurones: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Retina of eye
- [ ] B) Olfactory mucosa of nose
- [ ] C) Inner ear vestibular and cochlear organs
- [ ] D) Cerebral cortex
- [ ] E) Dorsal root ganglion

> **✅ Answers (Multiple Select):** A) Retina of eye, B) Olfactory mucosa of nose, C) Inner ear vestibular and cochlear organs
> **Explanation:** Bipolar neurones occur in retina, olfactory mucosa, and inner ear.
